notes.title: Eternal Live Balance Update – 10/2/2024
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/2115aae2e663d7f2807de2adf457938bb8e13bf7.png[/img]


This new balance patch is all about draft! We’re making targeted adjustments to 11 Key Cards to shake up the format and breathe new life into your Draft experience! Our goal is to elevate underrepresented factions and ensure every pick, strategy, and draw matters. 

[h1]Draft Buffs[/h1]
The upcoming adjustments bring fresh potential to some overlooked cards, empowering players with new tactical potions and revitalizing strategies across the board. Moreover, with these changes, struggling factions gain the resilience they need to stand strong against early-game attackers, Nomads, and damage-based removal. Stormwatcher, for instance, now serves as a steadfast Primal defender, making it a formidable obstacle against aggressive attacks and targeted removal, not to mention a valuable asset in your arsenal!

[list]
[*] Stormwatcher to 2/4 (from 0/5)
[*] Sparrow Augur gains Flying
[*] Cobalt Beetle to 2/3 (from 2/2)
[*] Called Shot to 3 cost (from 4 cost)
[*] Daring Pathcutter to 4/5 (from 4/3)
[*] Amethyst Beetle to 2/3 (From 2/2)
[*] New Prey to 4 cost (from 5 cost)
[*] Frontier Scout to 2/3 (from 2/2)
[*] Infamous Huntress to 2/2 (from 1/2)
[*] Chameleon Hide to 2/2 (from 1/3)
[/list]
Since Stormwatcher and Chameleon Hide are getting streamlined with reduced health, we are offering a Shiftstone refund for crafted copies!

[h1]Draft Nerf[/h1]
In addition to the buffs to help Shadow and Primal, we have one targeted nerf to an overperforming card that has contributed to the increased presence of Fire and Recruit in the top-performing decks.

[list]
[*] Tandem Strike to 3 cost with “One of your units Hunts 1. Recruit.” (Was 4 cost and “Hunts 2”)[/list]

Crafted copies of Tandem Strike will be eligible for a Shiftstone refund.

The changed cards hail from both [i]Behemoths of Thera[/i] and [i]Battle Lines[/i], so you can encounter these changes throughout your drafting journey. . How will you adjust your strategies when these updated cards appear in your draft picks? We can’t wait to see what you come up with! 


[h1]ICYMI: Chapter Books[/h1]
Hope you are caught up on your reading for Chapter Books 1 & 1 because Chapter Books 3 & 4 hit the digital shelves today!

As a reminder: Each book will unlock 6 past chapters for play as well as immediately grant each chapter’s avatar and 4x copies of the premium cards. If you already have the premium cards, you’ll receive extra copies which can be destroyed for shiftstone. To get the non-premium versions of the cards, you’ll have to play through the chapter as normal.

notes.title: Eternal Hotfix—June Hotfix
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/bf2845061aed6cdb7194f24de54c78e7d9b98e0e.png[/img]

We’re rolling out a fresh hotfix, perfect for the summer heat! Expect a range of improvements, including multiple bug fixes and card triggers. [i]Happy gaming![/i]


[h2]Bug Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where Master Archivist could crash the game when Inscribing Sureshot or Rakano Sheriff
[*] Fixed an issue where Execution Pit lost its link to the killed unit early after any Devour
[*] Fixed an issue where Tayana, the Mender could trigger repeatedly when discarding to a full hand
[*] Fixed an issue where Severin, the Hermit could play 0-health units, causing a loop if both players had Severin
[*] Fixed an issue where Steelfang Glaive copied strength from static effects, causing it to double apply
[*] Fixed an issue where Quick Study could gain too much of a stackable skill when multiple were played simultaneously
[*] Fixed an issue where Cunning Plan didn’t trigger Skullhaven Tinker or Eris, Apex Slayer’s Renown
[*] Fixed an issue where Tripwire Trap and Preyscouter triggering at the same time could make a unit briefly appear dead then return to play
[*] Fixed an issue where the Sashenka, Bound avatar didn’t display correctly
[*] Fixed an issue where Feral Centipede didn’t display its Killer on the Chapter outro screen
[/list]

notes.title: Eternal: Separate Ways ⛰️ – Rekindle Your Journey!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/eb1e3f23275da483e5ee3de028d89c026a257846.png[/img]

It’s time to dive back into the world of [i]Eternal[/i] with a brand-new adventure that promises more victory and more thrills! [i]Separate Ways[/i] brings a fresh twist and 25 exciting new cards to your collection.

[h1]The Story Continues...[/h1]
The Skycrag Six is no more. Krogar has fallen, and Sashenka is now enthralled under The Hermit’s dark magic. But the fight isn't over yet… The remaining heroes, though heavy-hearted, have split up to Thera’s major settlements, rallying the people to unify against The Hermit’s monstrous army of beasts and cultists. The resistance begins anew!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/d14895d7a77971ee17b9d0a86ec409fdfb50e1b8.png[/img]

[list]

[u]Not sure if the Legendary Bundle is right for you? We’ve got options:[/u]
[b]Separate Ways Bundle:[/b] For 1,000 Gems or 25,000 Gold, get 4 copies of each new card plus the Premium Avatar.
[b]Separate Ways Premium Bundle:[/b] For 2,000 Gems, score four premium and regular copies of each new card, the Premium Avatar, and four premium and regular copies of the New Alternate-Art of Finest Hour. 

And don’t worry—if you start with the [i]Separate Ways[/i] Bundle, you can upgrade to the Premium Bundle later for just 1,000 Gems!

[b]Ready to Rejoin the Battle?[/b]
The time has come to rally once more. Order [i]Separate Ways[/i] now and be among the first to experience this thrilling new chapter in [i]Eternal.[/i] Whether you're a returning champion or a hero seeking redemption, your adventure awaits!

See you on the battlefield! 🌟

notes.title: Eternal Live Balance Update – 4/24/2024
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/017b1d3a19dab624b329b484d754c9038c51ddde.png[/img]

[h1]Introduction[/h1]
Introducing the latest balance patch for Eternal—and this one’s geared towards draft aficionados! In this week’s update, we are taking a broad approach and making light adjustments to a full 20 cards, aimed at creating a refreshed draft meta where every card counts and your strategic expertise reigns supreme! 

[h2]Expedition Tweaks[/h2]
Of course, we couldn’t leave Expedition hanging so here are two staples we’re adjusting: 

[list]
[*] Calm Instructor loses Charge, gains Quickdraw
[*] Grove Supplier to 0/2 (was 1/2)
[/list]
Expedition is in a healthy place overall right now, but we’re still seeing a few decks with higher win rates than we like. To address this, we’re implementing some changes targeting aggressive Fire-based decks intended to reduce their raw damage while adding some strategic depth. 

Calm Instructor as a 2/1 Quickdraw in the deck generates a lot of opportunities for bluffing and increasing the utility of fast damage spells. Meanwhile, tweaking some of Grove Supplier’s strength prompts opposing players to make more nuanced decisions about whether to prioritize eliminating the Supplier or the units it enhances, rather than defaulting to targeting the Supplier every time. 

[h2]Draft Buffs[/h2]
The following adjustments are designed to inject some spice into the meta while also supporting specific factions and archetypes that may be lagging behind. 

[list]
[*] Sandspout Mirage to 3T (was 4T)
[*] Steelwarren Tunneler gains Endurance 
[*] Lured Songbird costs 4 less if a relic went to your void this turn (was 3 less)
[*] Rebellious Mistral to 5JJ (was 6JJ)
[*] Infamous Huntress to 1/2 (was 1/1)
[*] Hand of the Hecaton’s Summon is now, “You may sacrifice a unit to Hunt 3.” (was Hunt 2)
[*] Vizier’s Tablet ’s ability gains, “After the fifth use, Vizier Tablet’s sacrifice and draw a card of your choice from their void.”
[*] Warren Spymistress’s Bolster to +2 Strength (was +1 Strength).
[*] Telia's Choice now gives +3/+3 (was +2/+2)
[/list]

[h2]Influence Nerfs[/h2]
The following cards are all having a single point of influence requirement added:

[list]
[*] Hive Lantern to 2FF (was 2F)
[*] Liquid Flame to 3FF (was 3F)
[*] Beekeeper to 3TT (was 3T)
[*] Druid of the Sands to 4TT (was 4T)
[*] Charming Steelguard to 3JJ (was 3J)
[*] Prepared Tracker to 3JJ (was 3J)
[*] Changeestik to 2PP (was 2P)
[*] Nocturnal Glider to 3PP (was 3P)
[*] Extinguish to 3SS (was 3S)
[/list]

We’re happy that multifaction decks have been such a hit in Battle Lines draft, but right now decks that run all the best cards across 4-5 factions are completely dominating more focused 2-3 faction archetypes. By increasing the influence requirements of some key commons and uncommons, we hope to create more impactful drafting decisions and increase deck diversity.

As always, we thank you for your continued support and can’t wait to see what you do!

Get ready for some spring cleaning with this March Hotfix!

In this update, we’ve tidied up your game experience by addressing some AI issues and enhancing various quality-of-life features. Let’s dive in!

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where granting very large quantities of battle skills could cause the game to lag or crash
[*] Fixed an issue where Cunning Plan didn’t work with Renown abilities that scale on Cost
[*] Fixed an issue where your relic weapon would also die when a Versatile weapon on a unit was killed
[*] Fixed an issue where Zephyrus could trigger from units being targeted out of play
[*] Fixed an issue where cards transformed into Firebombs by Incendiary Slagmite could be missing Destiny
[*] Fixed an issue where Gravity Rifle didn’t apply its effects
[*] Fixed an issue where Duel for Steelwarren did nothing if your unit left play in response

[*] Fixed an issue where Glorious Gathering could fail to trigger the first turn you had 5 suitable heroes
[*] Fixed an issue where Listening Bug’s Summon didn’t offer a response window
[*] Fixed an issue where Rift Disaster’s card draw could be affected by Inspire units that were killed
[*] Fixed an issue where Invitation was not drawn at end of turn by Tayana, the Mender

[*] Fixed an issue where Telia, Skullhaven Steward required discarding before drawing cards from other copies attacking at the same time
[*] Fixed an issue where Marshal Ironthorn didn’t copy the Depleted state of power played by effects
[*] Fixed an issue where 0-strength units affected by Stoneskin were unable to use Killer
[*] Fixed an issue where Archgryffyn Patriarch and other Curse-counting effects didn’t update when Stakeout was played
[*] Fixed an issue where Alu, Death-Dreamer and other Curse-triggered effects didn’t trigger when curses were created and played by some effects
[*] Fixed an issue where Rift Siphon’s effect could trigger during the response window before the curse had resolved
[*] Fixed an issue where Sampa, “Elder” Advisor could fail to draw the spell that played a copy of Sampa
[*] Fixed an issue where Morbid Deal could fail to trigger some effects that trigger on unit death
[*] Fixed an issue where Nomad was not listed in the battle skills Glossary entry
[*] Fixed an issue where the Battle for the Throne achievement was not triggering correctly
[*] Fixed an issue where the AI would play Huddle Together for no value

[*] Fixed an issue where the AI would target poorly with Spellcraft

notes.title: Eternal Balance Update — 1/31
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/34b814cc5b3d82c2c3996f0e99a7da3ad714e4fb.png[/img]

Welcome to the first balance patch of the new year! 

This patch is heavily Expedition-focused, targeting some outliers to bring them more in line.  

[h1]Nerfs[/h1]
[list]
[*] The Winter Fox to 10-cost, -1 cost for every 2 cards you have Hunted (was 12-cost, -1 cost for every card you have Hunted).
[*] Corrupted Riftborn to 5/4 (was 5/5).
[*] Light the Beacon to 5-cost (was 4-cost).
[*] Deeptrail Vanguard now 2/4 and grants the drawn spell Voidbound (was 2/5).
[*] Unstable Hellion loses Overwhelm.
[/list]

The Winter Fox is an exciting quest, but can lead to uninteractive and one-sided games when it comes down too early. Decreasing the maximum cost while reducing the speed of the discount should keep it in a healthier range, while increasing the impact of Advantages gained from hunting.

Corrupted Riftborn, Deeptrail Vanguard, and Light the Beacon all have strategic gameplay we believe in, but their current rates have led them to be more dominant than we’d like. These changes should reduce their ubiquity while leaving them as viable options for decks that want to build around them.

Unstable Hellion’s Overwhelm has often meant that if you don’t have an answer to it immediately, you’re dead. Drawing a blocker to trade with the Hellion on its second attack often still meant taking 15 damage to your face. Removing the Overwhelm preserves the gameplay of maximizing its Emtomb damage while making blockers a more viable defensive option.

[h1]Buffs[/h1]
[list]
[*] Gold Mine to 2-cost (was 3-cost)
[*] Duel for Steelwarren to 5-cost (was 6-cost)
[*] Fiera, On the Frontlines to 5-cost (was 6-cost)
[*] One Eye Returned to 3/5 (was 3/4)
[*] Champion of Vengeance to 4/4 (was 3/3)
[*] Reeve's Mandate gains “Can’t be negated.”
[*] Insatiable Gorger to 4-cost (was 5- cost)
[/list]

These are a variety of changes intended to buff underperforming archetypes or inspire new avenues of exploration. The Reeve’s Mandate change in particular should provide more counterplay to the many powerful negate effects that are currently seeing play. 

Deeptrail Vanguard is in The Devouring set and Unstable Hellion was recently introduced in the Community Bundle. Players will receive 1,250 gold if they bought the base bundles and an additional 1,250 gold if they bought the premium versions. Corrupted Riftborn premiered in December 2023’s Eternal Chapter – Riftbreakers; players who purchased that chapter will receive 650 gold. All other crafted cards that are receiving a nerf can be destroyed for a full refund.

You can check out hover-over card images on our [url=https://news.direwolfdigital.com/eternal-balance-update-1-31/]news site[/url]: this patch will be live later today and we will update the forums accordingly.

[i]Happy playing!
[/i]

notes.title: Eternal — Merry Buffmas Patch Notes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/d64b551d057738a0e70700dddce78cdc1a9d42c5.png[/img]

[i]Eternals—[/i]
Get ready for a pretty big Hotfix, chock-full of improvements and bug-fixes to fine-tune your Eternal experience. First things first, Buffmas has come early! When we nerf a card due to its performance in Expedition, that can often push it out of Throne as well. We want to take this opportunity to revert a bunch of changes for cards that are no longer in Expedition and might be fun additions to the Throne metagame. 

[list]
[*] Phoenix Stone costs 2 to activate (was 3)
[*] Soulfire Drake to 5FFF (was 6FFF)
[*] Helena, Skyguide to 3/4 and +3/+4 (was 3/3 and +1/+1)
[*] Scalesworn Patrol gains Inscribe
[*] Vine Tangler costs 7 to activate (was 9)
[*] Slumbering Stone now plays the 2/2 Gargoyle on Entomb (was draw a 2/2 Gargoyle)
[*] Heart of the Vault to 6/6 (was 5/5)
[*] Acclaimed Artisan to Mastery 4 (was Mastery 6)
[*] The Bandit Queen to 3/3 (was 3/2)
[*] Eremot’s Machinations to 5TS (was 6TTSS)
[*] The Merriest Mandrake to 0/4 (was 0/3)
[/list]

However, alongside these joyous buffs, there is one particular card that’s been causing some problems of late. Spire Shadows has always been an interesting buildaround, but a dangerous and often uninteractive amount of cost reduction. The recent addition of the Recruit mechanic has pushed the deck to high popularity. While its win rate has remained relatively average due to weak aggro matchups, it preys heavily on midrange decks and has been reducing variety in the Throne metagame. 

[list]
[*] [i]Spire Shadows[/i] becomes a Relic with “Once per turn, when you draw a unit with higher cost than Strength, swap them.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/0a64c71d48b538548a9ed806ae09c70acf3df8a6.png[/img]

We experimented with a variety of changes, but just increasing the cost or making it a relic pushed the deck even more towards trying to set up a big combo turn without giving the opponent a chance to interact. This version maintains the low cost to start benefiting early, but increases counterplay and limits Recruit and Market shenanigans. Note that multiple copies in play trigger separately, so having three will swap the first three appropriate units you draw each turn.

[h3]Note: As Spire Shadows was only available through the set, Shadow of the Spire set, we are giving a one-time grant of 1,250 gold to users who purchased the set. Users that purchased the premium versions of the set will receive an additional 1,250 gold. Users will, of course, keep all their copies of the cards.[/h3]

[h1]Bug Fixes:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where The Hermit’s Triumph did not play VFX to the chosen units
[*] Fixed an issue where The Hermit’s Triumph could return a unit to the previous owner when you sacrificed one of them early
[*] Fixed an issue where some abilities that count things in the void did not immediately update after Devour effects
[*] Fixed an issue where some Devour cards’ superhinting didn’t update when new targets became present
[*] Fixed an issue where some abilities that count relics in the void didn’t update when a unit-equipped Versatile weapon entered the void
[*] Fixed an issue where Aerial Suppression could retain double damage when Flying units were removed from play
[*] Fixed an issue where Eris, Apex Slayer’s Renown could bypass Aegis
[*] Fixed an issue where Nomnom, Epic Epicure could die when discarding Poacher’s Menagerie
[*] Fixed an issue where Mystical Shackles’ summon could trigger twice when played from the void
[*] Fixed an issue where Bounty Board had no VFX and could sometimes trigger and resolve in the middle of combat animations
[*] Fixed an issue where Bounty Board was not triggered by Killer attacks
[*] Fixed an issue where Eyes of the Hermit didn’t reveal the top card of your deck when played by Recruit. 
[*] Fixed an issue where Hunts caused by Living Reflection could bypass Aegis in certain scenarios
[*] Fixed an issue where Reeking Troublemaker could prevent units from blocking if killed/silenced/transformed in response to its summon
[*] Fixed an issue where a stolen Ossuar Longbow would not gain armor from Hunting
[*] Fixed an issue where Cirt, Prime Deserter instantly died when created directly into play
[*] Fixed an issue where Cunning Plan’s sacrifice did not trigger Renown on your unit
[*] Fixed an issue where Cunning Plan’s sacrifice occurred after the enemy response window instead of before
[*] Fixed an issue where Tight-Lipped prevented Cunning Plan from sacrificing a unit
[*] Fixed an issue where Destiny units targeted by Altruistic Bonepicker or Against the Odds could keep their damage after dying
[*] Fixed an issue where Strip for Parts could not play Bloodrite Kalis
[*] Fixed an issue where Veli, Always Watching’s Bolster ability played VFX for the larger debuff first when doubled by Fiera, on the Frontlines
[*] Fixed an issue where Devour units could still buff themselves if they were killed in response. The Devour will still destroy cards if possible.
[*] Fixed an issue where Embargo Officer didn’t prevent Information Leak’s discard
[*] Fixed an issue where Voice of the Speaker did not grant Echo to power cards that were created and drawn
[*] Fixed an issue where Heirloom Blade could be partially played with 2-5 power and only shifted units in play
[*] Fixed an issue where Kosul Elite didn’t grant Fast to Versatile weapons
[*] Fixed an issue where Martyr’s Chains didn’t trigger unless there was at least one unit before a unit is created at the end of the turn
[*] Fixed an issue where Dizo’s Racket did not properly apply Lifesteal from relic weapons
[*] Fixed an issue where Blood of Makkar did not offer a response window when played
[*] Fixed an issue where some ongoing void-binding abilities did not update when stolen
[*] Fixed an issue where Vara, Decisive Action could be sacrificed by Vara, Death’s Master
[*] Fixed an issue where Can’t Remember showed the enemy deck when they had Aegis
[/list]

[h2]Improvements:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated Fang Trap’s functionality so that the Bolster debuff can stack correctly with existing damage on the unit. It now grants a permanent debuff to the cursed unit, rather than modifying the curse’s ongoing debuff amount.
[*] Updated Vulk’s Heart so that it can play a Vulk with 0 or less health if the +2/+2 will get Vulk above 0 health
[*] Streamlined VFX for all spells with Unleash to play faster, especially Growth Spurt
[*] Removed outdated Black Market hangers on Rime Conclave Smuggler and Fearless Crescendo
[*] Updated spell-negating abilities like Numbing Cold to not trigger against spells that cannot be negated
[/list]

notes.title: Balance Update and Patch Notes 11.8.2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/f88a85119a02f54881f3d3860797e894e3339dcd.png[/img]

Welcome to the first post-[i]Battle Lines[/i] live balance patch!

The primary focus of this patch is [b]Draft[/b], but we’re making some small Expedition-targeted changes as well.

[h2]Expedition
[/h2][list]
[*] Lipa, Witch of the Woods to 1/1 (was 2/1)
[*] Karrina, Embercaster to 3/3 (was 4/3
[*] Kid, Grove's Heart to 3/2 (was 3/3)
[*] Turnabout now deals 2 damage even if the unit wasn’t played this turn. (Still 6 damage if the unit was played this turn, was no damage otherwise.)
[/list]

Lipa’s base rate has been high enough to see play in almost every Primal Expedition deck, from the most aggressive to the most controlling. And that’s before you start taking advantage of her synergies with Mirror Image, General Fiera, or the new Devour mechanic. Losing a point of power should reduce her ubiquity and speed at closing out games while leaving her a viable option for decks that take particular advantage of her.

Charge-heavy strategies with Kid, Grove’s Heart have also proven to be a bit too fast and resilient, capable of racing down opponents who stumble even slightly. We don’t want to be too heavy-handed while the new metagame is developing, but minor nerfs to Kid and Karrina should allow a little more room for new strategies to emerge.

Turnabout was designed to be a strong answer to these Charge-heavy strategies, but the weakness of the base use has been too limiting to succeed in that role. We’re raising the floor while making sure it’s still at its best when used tactically against Charge, Killer, and Ambush.

[h2]Draft
[/h2]
[list]
[*] Aerial Suppression to 2-cost (was 1-cost)
[*] Fireguide to 2/4 (was 4/4)
[*] Contraption Crafter to 1/3 (was 0/4)
[*] Forked Lightning to 2-cost (was 3-cost)
[*] Cunning Plan to 5SS non-fast (was 7SS Fast)
[*] Putrefying Presence gains “Draw a card.”
[*] Sonic Blast to 2-cost (was 3-cost)
[*] Glory Seeker Renown bonus now grants +1/+1 and Lifesteal (was just Lifesteal)
[/list]

[i]Please note these images will be updated to reflect changes later today.
[/i]

Fire has been overperforming in draft while Shadow has been lagging in last place. We’re taking two fire commons down a notch, giving Primal some better options for fighting against Nomad, and buffing several shadow commons and uncommons.

Shadow’s Renown archetype was struggling in particular, so most of our buffs are focused there. We had intentionally aimed low with Putrefying Presence, with the goal of being a low-power Renown enabler that wouldn’t get scooped up by other decks. In practice, Renown has had plenty of enablers but hasn’t paid off enough when its game plan comes together.

Along with these balance update, we’re also fixing a lot of bugs that were found:

[h2]Bug Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where Fiera, On the Frontlines didn’t apply to Ziat, Whatever It Takes and Veli, Always Watching.
[*] Fixed an issue where Insatiable Gorger could be triggered by enemy Devour effects
[*] Fixed an issue where Quinn, Skullhaven Warden’s buff didn’t persist through zone changes or unit copying
[*] Fixed an issue where Theran Sniper’s debuff didn’t persist through zone changes or unit copying
[*] Fixed an issue where Telia, Perfect Timing’s Ultimate did not trigger if she died while hitting the enemy player
[*] Fixed an issue where Skullhaven Tinker and Eris, Apex Slayer didn’t trigger by weapons created into play
[*] Fixed an issue where Devoted Ranger didn’t draw a card when triggered by weapons created into play
[*] Fixed an issue where Theran Sniper could apply -0/-0 when triggered by Inscribe spells
[*] Fixed an issue where Veli, Always Watching didn’t increase its ability if the target left play in response
[*] Fixed an issue where Shockwave Elemental could attempt to stun units with Endurance
[*] Fixed an issue where Strange Blacksmith and Strange Gladiator did not display VFX to their targets
[*] Fixed an issue where Vara, Decisive Action shared its import/export number with Scared Beetender 
[/list]


[i]-Happy Playing
[/i]

notes.title: Battle Lines: Devour!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/a4b51ce274cc73c483865c96f3fe831e5b08e4da.png[/img]

[i]My beasts are hungry. Wherever you Nomads roam, and whether you Bolster your ranks with new Recruits or you rely on the Renowned skill of your trained warriors, my beasts will Devour you all.
[/i]

Welcome to the last preview article for Battle Lines! We’ve gone over four different mechanics for four different tri-faction sides in the fight against The Hermit. But where has The Hermit himself been all this time? What does he have to offer?

Wonder no more, as The Hermit’s beast army is represented by Primal, Fire, and Shadow, and is composed of, well, beasts (And The Hermit himself)! And their mechanic is Devour, which will only be found in these factions in[i] Battle Lines[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/68dafae9ff28b7e62517d0e0bd581c4f29c2ae0c.png[/img]

[b]Devour X: Effect[/b] means, “When played, you may destroy that many cards from the top of the enemy void to get the listed effect.”

Cards that have been Devoured are completely removed from the game forever. So playing Voltaic Viper will remove the opponent’s ability to interact with the top 2 cards of their void permanently while netting you a card in the process.

To get into the nitty gritty a little, the ability won’t happen if you don’t meet the Devour threshold, and Voidbound cards cannot be Devoured and will be skipped over. The enemy player can respond to Devour abilities. If they protect their void with Aegis or remove enough cards in response, it will prevent your Devour ability entirely.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/bba7210a325a091a9f412093ffb7ecae88aefd94.png[/img]

[b]Devour[/b] can also appear on attachments, like Stalker Spear. A 2/2 Versatile weapon is fine and all, but if you can wait until you can devour 4 cards, you get a permanent +2/+2 stat increase. Perfect on either your avatar to take out a medium sized threat, or on a unit to make a truly formidable beater!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/16f666f70c4d6b9f703ff87231ab861ad4aaba43.png[/img]

Meanwhile [i]Insatiable Gorger[/i] gives you a little bit more bang for your buck. Whether it or another card is the one doing the Devouring, this greedy little creature can undergo quite the growth spurt.

And that will do it for the preview articles for[b] Battle Lines[/b], coming out October 18th! If you haven’t yet, make sure to check out the pre-order news here, and come hang out with us in the official Discord!

What’s that? You want even more spoilers? Well, I suppose we can do one last one for the road…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/0cf617a953fba6d8549b31f2a902467d05d628bc.png[/img]

notes.title: Battle Lines: Nomad and Bolster!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/ea8c7469c4dc0cc967889ba6a2cc3587ffa48f43.png[/img]

[i]After the tragedy of Hivefall, the surviving Hivetenders have become Nomads, traveling Thera in caravans hoping to find a new place to rebuild. Meanwhile the citizens and soldiers of Steelwarren have been besieged by an army of beasts. Only by Bolstering their defenses will they have a chance to survive.
[/i]

Welcome to the second of three preview articles for [i]Battle Lines[/i]. Last time we looked at two of the major mechanics that [i]Battle Lines[/i] has to offer. And today there are two more to look at!

Let’s start with Time, Fire, and Justice, the factions representing The Hive Caravan. The Caravan is formed by Hivetenders, Lanterns, and Mistrals, and they bring a new battle skill to the table: Nomad. You’ll only find Nomad in these factions in Battle Lines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/f9180b2eb61b7bfa4cf853bfe0ef98dce82cc91e.png[/img]

[b]Nomad [/b]is a battle skill that is always followed by a number. Nomad X means "This unit has Flying on your turn and +X/+X on the enemy turn.”

So [b]Hexamancer[/b] is a 2/2 Flyer on your turn, but a 4/4 ground unit on the opponent’s turn. Great for attacking or for blocking, but you have to choose which you’d prefer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/55b207b417659648a05bae3fa7267bf6590a9268.png[/img]

When you give Nomad to a unit that already has Nomad, you add the values together. Playing Pilgrim's Pack on a unit with Nomad 1, it’ll become a unit with Nomad 3. If you play another, it’ll jump up to Nomad 5! That’s a lot of extra stats to have on your blockers!

And adding [b]Nomad[/b] to a unit with Flying will cause it to gain the stats on the opponent’s turn without it losing Flying. The same is true if giving Flying to a unit with Nomad.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/06e383a2515da9331b4e796a30b0664db2684792.png[/img]

Normally[b] Nomad[/b] gives you the choice of having an evasive attacker, or an efficient defender. But with Queenguard Elite’s Endurance, you can do both! Soar over your opponent’s defenses on your turn, then turn away their onslaught on theirs!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/a4b51ce274cc73c483865c96f3fe831e5b08e4da.png[/img]

Lastly, we have Steelwarren represented by Justice, Time, and Shadow. Steelwarren is composed of Fiera’s soldiers, Ziat’s enforcers, and the people’s rebellion headed by Dran. And their mechanic Bolster will be found exclusively within their factions in Battle Lines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/4ef9bf40f75586ffa1fcb3333cb54ab658008050.png[/img]

[b]"Bolster: Effect"[/b] is a game term that means "Once per turn, when you gain Health or Armor, do the listed effect."

In Charming Steelguard’s case, this means playing a 1/2 Aegis unit the first time you gain Health or Armor. The next time you gain Health or Armor that turn, The Steelguard will fail to enlist anyone, but he’ll be ready again on the next person’s turn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/5f73d49eb0088b1497effa6a28eae61e0b859bb7.png[/img]

Like [b]Recruit[/b], [b]Bolster[/b] can appear on all sorts of card types. Fang Trap may not reduce the enemy unit’s stats by much on its own… but trigger Bolster a few times and they’ll soon find themselves unable to stand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/f19b71705e27063001cdd4842bf4a83b81f2323f.png[/img]


Ziat’s very busy now trying to keep the people of Steelwarren safe. What better way to do that than by just killing anything that threatens them?

How will you handle The Hermit’s beast army? Will you Bolster yourself with plenty of Health and Armor to withstand the onslaught? Or will you embrace a Nomadic lifestyle, to have the tactical advantage over your enemies? Make your choice soon, as [i]Battle Lines[/i] comes out on [url=https://news.direwolfdigital.com/eternal-battle-lines-%e2%9a%94%ef%b8%8f/]October 18th![/url]

notes.title: Battle Lines: Renown & Recruit!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/e4b5927dd05b94f5dbdc4c432957c3b78d29431e.png[/img]

[i]Ever since the events of Hivefall, the former rogues’ den of Skullhaven has become a place of great Renown, bringing in refugees while its people fight against The Hermit’s beasts. Meanwhile the Youngbloods Recruit everyone they can, hoping to keep their grove and way of life safe.
[/i]
Welcome to the first of three preview articles for [i]Battle Lines[/i], Eternal’s newest set! [i]Battle Lines[/i] is a set heavily focused on the five alliances that have risen in Thera after the fall of The Hive. Each is represented by three different factions, and each with its own mechanic found exclusively within those factions.

Let’s start with Skullhaven. Skullhaven is composed primarily of Bonepickers, Rangers, and Slayers, all groups known across Thera for their daring and dangerous trades. As such, their mechanic is Renown, which will be found exclusively in Shadow, Justice, and Primal in Battle lines!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/4083627a8cee74e4aaf55da2af34e5a548f3f457.png[/img]

[b]Renown[/b] is a returning mechanic we’ve not seen since all the way back in Defiance. For those who weren’t playing Eternal then, or just need a refresher, Renown means “The first time you play a spell or weapon on this unit, do the following.”

Basically, Renown gives you or your units a bonus whenever you play something on them. In the case of Daring Pathcutter, you’ll get an Aegis and draw a card. That’s some good value!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/58a3674792f5bf2902e420e23fece57c39018e21.png[/img]

Canny Hunter adds a new twist to Renown. By Ambushing it in and then playing a fast spell like [i]Finest Hour[/i] on it, you can completely turn an opponent’s attack upside down! And this is just the start of the tricky things you can do with Renown.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/4d968c0c3040ad4843aa865f6510c9bae9c62f48.png[/img]

Some Renown cards care about the cost of the spell or weapon played on them. Eris in particular is very interested in your most expensive spells or weapons, so how deep are your pockets?

Next up is the Grove Alliance, represented by Fire, Time, and Primal. It’s composed of the Youngblood Exiles, the Druids, and you might see an occasional appearance from the Skycrag Six! They’re looking to protect The Grove from the Hermit’s beast army, and are looking to Recruit anyone they can to do it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/570e99a4e33873bcbe91fc76268e837025e55c3d.jpg[/img]


[b]Recruit [/b]is a game action that means “Draw a unit from the top five cards of your deck. If it costs less than this card, play it. Bottom the rest.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/3eb66b83568fedfeedcb081dbecad12c5bfccd72.png[/img]

If you play Calm Instructor and in the top 5 cards of your deck there’s a Twilight Lantern, and a Gnarled Ant, you could choose to draw either. If you choose the Lantern, you’ll then immediately play it from your hand as it costs less than Calm Instructor. Which is more important to your gameplan?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/528ebf817834bb8e23240272a07f4b500249c471.png[/img]

You may also find a handful of cards within the Grove Alliance that have Inspire, which synergizes perfectly with Recruit. You always draw the unit you Recruit, even if you then immediately play it, so it will always benefit from the Inspire buff! Patrice’s ability to do both will no doubt serve the Grove well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/528ebf817834bb8e23240272a07f4b500249c471.png[/img]

So who will you choose to bring at your side in battle? The renowned fighters of Skullhaven? Or the fresh new recruits from the Grove? Make your choice when Battle Lines comes out October 18th!


Units aren’t the only thing that can Recruit; spells and attachments can as well! Grove Defenses can stun enemies to pave the way for your attackers, while also Recruiting a new unit to your cause. Make use of the opening and push through!

notes.title: Eternal Live Balance Update - 7/19/2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/7e8c9263fab9b3e202a37b8c09b56827f10927e7.png[/img]

Greetings from Thera! It’s been a few months since[i] The Devouring[/i], and while we’re overall happy with its impact on the meta, we’re making a few small balance changes aimed primarily at Expedition.


[list]
[*]Riftfeeder Wasp to “Empower: +2/+2.” and “Summon: Draw two random power cards from your deck…” (was “Empower: +3/+3.” and “Summon: Draw the top two power cards of your deck.”)[/list]
Riftfeeder Wasp has been a flashpoint for discussion since it was released. We like the decision points it creates and the way it can outscale board stalls, but we agree that it can kill a little too quickly without providing enough space for the opponent to respond. It can often end the game in two attacks, hitting for 9 the turn after it’s played and 12 the turn after that. We want to keep its ability to scale up over time but pull back on how quickly that happens. It was also getting some hidden power by improving your upcoming draws in addition to the threatening body and power cards up front.

[list]
[*] Kelmak's Bloodspear now gains Voidbound when played from the void. [/list]
It’s been cool to have a recurring Versatile weapon that can be played on a unit one time and as a relic the next, but the abundance of cheap heroes in Throne has made it trivial to recur numerous times in a single game. Star-Reader Severin has been a particular offender, which is ironic given the circumstances of Kelmak’s death. This change retains the ability to recur the Spear in either of its forms, but creates a point where your opponent can stop worrying about it.

[list]
[*] Foxfang Katars to 4/2 (was 3/2)[/list]
Foxfang Katars have largely been overshadowed by Ossuar Longbow, even in Rakano decks that can easily meet the influence requirements. We believe that this buff will increase the variety in Expedition by giving Longbow a strong competitor with different upsides and restrictions.
[list]
[*] Youngblood Tactician to 3/3 (was 3/1)[/list]
Youngblood Tactician is an appropriately tactical and dynamic way for Fire decks to fight through large Time blockers. While it’s already strong in those matchups, we wanted to improve its floor in other matchups with a bit of extra health.

[i]Note: As Rift Wasp and Kelmak’s Bloodspear were only available through The Devouring set, we are giving a one-time grant of 2,500 gold to users who purchased the set. Users that purchased the premium versions of the set will receive an additional 2,500 gold. Users will, of course, keep all their copies of the cards.[/i]

As always, we thank you for your continued support as we continue to evolve the meta!

notes.title: Eternal Live Balance 5-24-2023
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/c23c01e0a2e68e8f9f4daecf9d43db6015122e50.jpg[/img]

Gather round, heroes. The time has come for another Eternal Balance Update...

[list]
[*] Ascetic Lantern to 2-cost 2/2 (from 1-cost 2/1)
[*] Twilight Lantern to 1/3 (from 2/2)
[/list]
In Expedition, Fire-based aggro (including Stonescar) has crept up to a worrying win rate, especially at higher MMRs. While the two lanterns aren’t necessarily the most powerful cards in these decks, they do contribute significantly to many of the most despairing games. The increased health adds a bit more variety to Fire statlines and what blockers/removal line up most efficiently against them.

[list]
[*] "Save the Day" to “Kill an enemy unit without Endurance.” (was “Kill an enemy unit.)
[/list]

Save the Day serves a valuable metagame function as both a way to stabilize against aggressive decks and close out midrange mirrors. That said, it has become repetitive in that use, with too many games ending the same way. We’re adding a little more room for counterplay, so that units with Endurance can provide offense or defense through the AOE stun instead of just being target #1.

[list]
[*] "Youngblood Driver" to 4/4 (was 4/2)
[/list]

This is a fun little build-around who hasn’t seen much play. The extra health brings up the floor on casting it with 0-2 other spells, without substantially impacting the already impressive best-case scenarios.

Crafted copies of Ascetic Lantern and Twilight Lantern can be destroyed for a full refund. Because Save the Day is only obtained from a Chapter, players who purchased [i]Chapter 9 - The Long Path[/i] will receive a 650 gold grant. 

Thanks for your support, and thanks for playing Eternal!

[i]-The Eternal Team
[/i]

notes.content:

Today’s patch addresses a variety of bugs present in Unleashed. The full list of patch notes can be seen below.

[h2]Bug Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where Tota Pioneer could grant power more than once per turn
[*] Fixed an issue where Unleashed Reprints weren’t available for random creation/transformation in Draft.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Feed the Frenzy achievement could not be completed
[*] Fixed an issue where Sahin, Stateless didn’t trigger Lifesteal or Frenzy with its Summon damage
[*] Fixed an issue where Mystical Shackles’ summon occurred during the response window before it resolved
[*] Fixed an issue where Pin the Jotun selected the enemy unit after their response window
[*] Fixed an issue where Premium Riot Detail’s Summon didn’t function
[*] Fixed an issue where Gift of Xulta didn’t move to the enemy player when it copied a Cursed Relic
[*] Fixed an issue where Counting Room applied its effect during the response window before it resolved
[*] Fixed an issue where Counting Room didn’t prevent some Entomb abilities that draw from the void
[*] Fixed an issue where Cleave didn’t remove relic weapon armor before dealing damage
[*] Fixed an issue where Windscreamer’s permanent Flying was prevented by Harnessed Thrillseeker’s temporary Flying
[*] Fixed an issue where some cards triggered their own “when you play another unit” when played by Poacher’s Menagerie
[*] Fixed an issue where Fall of the Spire didn’t prevent cards from being played by some effects
[*] Fixed an issue where Unleash cards kept their red glow if they weren’t discarded at the end of the turn due to Genetrix Irel, Wayward
[*] Fixed an issue where Unleash cards lost their red glow when transformed
[*] Fixed an issue where cards that lost Unleash could not be reduced below 1 cost
[*] Fixed an issue where some new Help Tips and Glossary entries were missing or incomplete.
[*] Fixed a typo in the Create Unowned Cards dialog
[/list]

[h2]Card Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed localization issues with various cards
[*] Improved Eclipse’s hinting and dynamic text
[/list]

[h2]Known Issues:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Resonance Wave doesn’t have Inscribe as it should.
[*] Gift of Xulta functions incorrectly when copying Xenan Obelisk
[*] Blackmaw Carnosaur can gain/lose Lifesteal during battle damage.
[*] Genetrix Irel, Wayward’s stat buff applies before Unleash, unlike similar abilities.
[*] Halotipped Spray doesn’t remove relic weapon armor before it deals damage.
[*] Collaboration counts only one faction from each multifaction unit
[*] Sleight of Hand doesn’t transform power cards when triggers resulted from the draw
[*] Draconic Looting can prevent Unleash spells from creating copies
[*] Stutterstep doesn’t reinstall some abilities when the unit reappears
[/list]

As always, we appreciate your feedback and support as we continue to improve Eternal. If you encounter an issue or need help, please drop us a line at Support@DireWolfDigital.com so we can see what’s up.

If you’re enjoying Eternal, please take a moment to rate & review the game to help spread the word to other players!

notes.title: Revelations Balance Changes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/8b9c8a9e0b2024437fd0c003401f4b19dc38a53b.jpg[/img]

Welcome back! We hope you’ve been enjoying Revelations so far and we are looking forward to showing off the set more during the upcoming [url=https://direwolfdigital.com/news/revelations-5k-throne-open/][i]Revelations $5k Throne Open[/i][/url] beginning Friday, June 11th.

In advance of that, we’ve got a small handful of changes today, looking to shake things up a bit in the Throne format as well as Draft and Expedition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/0d66c9bf0f7a0989db2b2f1bbbf06341ca8701f5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Nerfs[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Sling of the Chi[/b] – Now “Enemies can’t transform your units” (was “enemies can’t transform your cards”)
[*][b]Rost, the Walking Glacier[/b] – No longer has Overwhelm
[*][b]Siege Breaker[/b] – No longer has Overwhelm
[/list]
An awesome reward for playing with some beefy units, we’ve heard the feedback of how challenging some players find the Sling decks to beat. For instance our primal players feel reliant on transformation like Formbend to help deal with pesky relics. While we like how Sling complements its monsters by shielding them from transformation, to help open up more options for counterplay, we’re removing its global transformation suppression and moving that ability to just units. Additionally, Sling decks often win by combining it with lots of big Overwhelm units so that summon damage spills over. It’s awesome for a unit build-around like Sling to work even better if your unit has the right skill, but right now, it’s so much of a freeroll in deckbuilding as nearly every unit players might want to combine with Sling has Overwhelm. By reducing how many big units there are with Overwhelm, players facing the Sling will get a better shot to defend themselves.

(Note: As Sling of the Chi is from a campaign, players who purchased the base version of the campaign will receive 1,250 gold and owners of the premium campaign will receive 2,500 gold.)

[list]
[*] [b]Grenahen[/b] – Now puts the unselected cards on the bottom of your deck (was discard)
[/list]
A nifty bird for players looking to stabilize against an aggressive start and find some tools for later on, and it’s proven to be also powerful combo enabler like with Felrauk and Elding. Being such great option to fight back against aggro and enabling explosive combo starts, we’re pulling back on how great the card is at so many jobs Moving the extra cards from the void to the bottom of the deck lets players who want to work to do something crafty with those void and discard combos continue to do so, but not in such an incidental way with Grenahen.

(Note: As Grenahen is from a campaign, players who purchased the base version of the campaign will receive 1,250 gold and owners of the premium campaign will receive 2,500 gold.)

[list]
[*] [b]Crafty Occultist[/b] – Now 3FFPP (was 3FP)
[/list]
A nifty jack of all trades, the Occultist delivers a bunch of options to Skcyrag players to help them smooth things out and still add to their board. Beyond that it’s been a big contributor to how much three and four faction discard related decks there are in the meta. As players continue to adapt and we monitor this,  it was clear the current incarnation of decks are really benefitting from how easily they can play great enablers and rewards from across the factions in one deck. By adding to the Occultist’s influence requirements, it’ll remain a great tool for Skycrag players but not so easy to slot into three and four-faction decks.

(Note: As Crafty Occultist is from a campaign, players who purchased the base version of the campaign will receive 1,250 gold and owners of the premium campaign will receive 2,500 gold.)

[list]
[*] [b]Azindel Revealed[/b] – Helici are now Factionless (were TS)
[/list]Reanimator decks have long focused on bringing back a Vara, Fate-Touched to then bring back Azindel, and then, Azindel’s Shadow-Time Helici to proc Vara again and fill their board with units from the void, virtually ending the game on the spot. With the rise of some new great void tools, it’s a good time to address the state of Reanimator. As we make new cards to bring units back like A Life From A Life, we could try to balance things around this one combo, but it’s a combo that’s had a lot of time in the sun. There’s a lot more that’s possible for void strategies if Vara and Azindel weren’t so dominant an option together. By making the mysterious Azindel’s Helici factionless, we’re preserving these cards as potential tools, pulling back on the wombo combo with Vara, and charting new space for Reanimator in Eternal for players to explore.

(Note: As Azindel Revealed is from a campaign, players who purchased the base version of the campaign will receive 1,250 gold and owners of the premium campaign will receive 2,500 gold.)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/0d66c9bf0f7a0989db2b2f1bbbf06341ca8701f5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Buffs[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Freight Asri[/b] – Now 2/4 (was 1/4)[/list]
As we continue to monitor the early developments of the Revelations Draft metagame, we’re giving a boost to a common from an underperforming faction.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/0d66c9bf0f7a0989db2b2f1bbbf06341ca8701f5.jpg[/img]

That’s all we’ve got for today, we’re very excited to see how things continue to develop with Revelations, and make sure to check out coverage for the $5k Throne Open on Sunday June 13th at twitch.tv/direwolfdigital!

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/254da11b9027215d9723fa1c3180de8d674935cc.jpg[/img]

[i]“Bastion still stands…” the Queen of Glass says flatly, standing at a high balcony to survey the wreckage that the storm left scattered across the Reach. The massive armored figure beside her remains silent, as always. She looks away. “Tch.”

“I suppose we’ve always known that it would come to this.” Her voice is distant – tinged with sadness, but resolved. “I had hoped that we could break the cycle…could create another way. If only the storm had done its work, it would have been a kindness.”

The heavy metallic sounds of repair and reconstruction have already begun in the square below. In Bastion, not a single day can be spared as the Shadowsea rises ever higher. The storm has passed, and now the great task of survival goes on.

She sighs. “We still have other methods – more direct – to do what must be done. And it is long past time.” The Queen of Glass steps away from the balcony rail. She does not beckon for the man to follow; she knows that he will, and he does.

“We’ve always known what the coming confrontation will cost me.” The woman reflexively touches the smooth porcelain mask that hides her face. “But we do have the advantage,” she muses as she slips into the grey shadows of the tower, “of also knowing how it will end.”[/i]

notes.title: 3/10 Live Balance Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/ff91125f89858f3f66f1d10a5d65fa392a74ba72.png[/img]

It’s good to be back! With the $5k [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2021-eternal-world-championship/]Stormbreak Throne Open[/url] just around the corner (March 26-28!), we have a few nerfs and buffs to [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/3-10-live-balance-update/]announce[/url] to shake things up a bit in both Throne and Expedition.

[h1]Nerfs[/h1]
[b][b]Bring to Justice [/b]– Now 1JJJ (was 0JJJ)[/b]

Bring to Justice has been a staple Market card in Justice since its release, allowing people access to a 0-cost kill spell under some specific circumstances. The combination with Rime-Conclave Smuggler in particular has given Hooru access to a very strong turn 3 on-curve removal play. This change will make that harder to pull off, while still allowing Justice decks to have a low-cost removal spell if they’re willing to put in the work.

[b]Winchest Merchant – Now 2/2 (was 2/3)[/b]

Winchest Merchant has proven to be the most popular way for people to use the Market in Expedition, and has been a fixture in Soldier decks in particular. We’re pulling back slightly on its rate to give people some incentives to explore other market options for those decks going forward.

[b]Krull, Xumuc Occultist – Now SS:[/b] When Krull damages a player, play a unit from their void with cost less than or equal to the damage dealt (previously no influence requirement)

Krull gives players a powerful void option that operates very differently from most other cards. While it’s a lot of fun to find a Krull at the exact right moment and fish up something powerful from your void, the community sentiment has been that it feels wrong for non-shadow decks to get this powerful effect without even being able to play Krull from their hand normally. This change should help maintain the faction pie a little better while still allowing Krull to do her thing in decks actually working for Shadow influence.

[h1]Buffs[/h1]
We also wanted to take this opportunity to buff some lesser-played cards, in particular focused on giving some upgrades to underplayed Throne cards, and a little love to a poor, maligned Grenadin.

[b]Brel, Solist Apostate[/b] – Now 6FFJJSS (was 7)

[b]Vargo Redclaw [/b]– Now 6/4 (was 5/4)

[b]Talir’s Unwinding[/b] – Now Fast

[b]Tavia, Lethrai Raidleader[/b] – Now 4 to activate (was 5)
[b]
Triumphant Stranger[/b] – Now plays a random Stranger at the end of your turn (was start of turn)

[b]Voprex, Hope’s End[/b] – Now permanently steals units

[b]Cryptic Master [/b]– Now 2/2 (was 1/1)
[b]
Gren, Iron Martyr[/b] – No longer a coward (Gren can now block)

[b]Lethrai Soothsayer [/b]– Now 3P (was 4)

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Grand Suppressor should no longer suppress Amplify abilities.
[*] Rhuus, Warbeast can no longer apply its buff to itself.
[*] Added “Dog” unit sub-type to Scrap Hound.
[*] Adjusted Inoa, Elevator Overseer to grant power first.
[*] Fixed some issues with Midchief Salus’s Amplify so that it works correctly with Jetpack and other effects that prevent playing spells.
[*] Improved translations for several cards.
[/list]

Be sure to check out the Throne format on display with the $5k Stormbreak Throne Open, with the event running March 26-28, and official coverage on March 28th where we’ll see who earns an invite to our 2021 World Championship! Make sure to follow and subscribe to notifications over at our Dire Wolf Digital Twitch account to get notified when the action begins on March 28th!

[url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/draft-packs-card-list/]Draft Packs and the Expedition format have been updated![/url]

In addition, today's patch 1.52.1 contains a variety of bug fixes and quality of life improvements listed below.

[h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Global Nav should now appear correctly on all screens.
[*]Cards should now always appear as expected when featured in a tutorial message.
[*]Fixed some visual layering issues with MOTD tiles.
[*]Fixed some issues with swipe-to-attack all responding too quickly, or not at all.
[*]Destiny prompts should no longer cover Scouted cards.
[*]Adjusted hangers so that they should fit on screen for cards like Lord Steyer’s Tower
[*]Fixed an issue where rapidly selecting attackers would cause visual issues with attack state.
[*]Deck tiles in Deck Select are no longer cropped strangely on mobile devices.
[*]Sling of the Chi will no longer break opponent’s Aegis when it is played.
[*]Dr. Zytrom now sacrifices selected units at the correct time when he was played at the end of a turn.
[*]Invasive Species can no longer be played via Bargain if Embargo Officer is in play

[*]The preview for the Witching Hour playmat has been restored.
[*]Fixed an issue where Xbox achievements released alongside the Awakening campaign were not unlocking properly.
[*]Fixed an issue where Steam achievements released alongside Buried Memories were not unlocking at all.
[/list]

[/i]
[h3]Card Updates:[/h3]
[list]

[h3]General Improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Improved appearance of the game on iPhone 12 mini devices.
[*]Improved appearance of Expedition format info on mobile devices.
[*]Added animations to show Market Exchanges more clearly.
[*]Improved controller navigation.
[*]Improved Deck Builder’s enforcement of Market rules.

notes.title: Buried Memories Preview Event!
notes.content:
Begin your exploration of Bastion's past in the [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/buried-memories-preview-event/]Buried Memories Preview Event[/url] - Live this weekend! 

Join us this weekend for a brand new Preview Event where you will be able to play with five new Preconstructed Theme decks, each with one new card from [i]Buried Memories[/i]! 

There is a special boss rule in play:

Each game you’ll begin with a relic in play that allows you to spend 2 power to draw a random unit of your deck’s tribe. Then, the cost increases by 2 for further activations.

The event costs 200 gems or 2500 gold to participate. You may run any number of times, but only your first five runs count on the leaderboard.

Here’s how it works:

[list]
[*] There are 5 specially-constructed theme decks – each containing one new card from [i]Buried Memories[/i]! 
[*] Each of your first 5 runs in the Event will use a different deck.
[*] After 5 entries into the Event, you will play with a deck selected at random.
[*] These decks are not added to your collection.
[*] This event costs 2,500 gold or 200 gems to enter.

notes.title: 2/1 Live Balance Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/f7d89580659141be1be9c9f2725acde81fd9e43d.png[/img]
https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2-1-live-balance-update/

Since the release of [i]Empire of Glass[/i] and the [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/1-8-live-balance-update/]1/8 Live Balance Update[/url], we have been carefully monitoring both the Throne and Expedition formats, and we have some [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2-1-live-balance-update/]changes[/url] that are sure to have a big impact on both going forward!


[url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2-1-live-balance-update/]Nerfs:[/url] 
[b]Heavy Artillery[/b]  – Now creates and draws a 3/3 Raildriver (was create and play)

Valkyrie-Warp has been a somewhat polarizing mechanic, creating some pretty exciting swings when you manage to pull it off at the opportune moment. With that comes the risk of things feeling unfair and like the game is snowballing out of control when the opponent manages to warp it early in the game. To that end, we’re changing Heavy Artillery to cut out some of the more extreme high-roll opportunities, while still preserving the core functionality of the card.

[b]The Speaking Circle [/b] – Now 3 durability (was 4) and “Kill enemy sites at the end of each turn” (Was “The enemy player can’t have a site”)

The Speaking Circle is a very different kind of site, and provides players with interesting and different choices every time it’s played. With that being said, the mirror matches with it can be very frustrating with the player who played their Speaking Circle first completely locking out their opponent. This change will allow for a bit more back-and-forth, while also making the powerful factionless site a bit easier to kill.

[b]Invasive Creeper[/b]  – Now 2/1 (was 2/2)

[b]Vine Tangler [/b] – Now 9 to Ultimate (was 7)

Mandrakes have still been incredibly powerful in the Expedition format, in particular Xenan-based mandrake decks that use ultimates to create very large and powerful boards. We’re making a pair of these mandrakes a little weaker to promote a bit more format diversity.

[b]Cylixes[/b] – Now require three of their faction before playing undepleted or creating a Trove (was two)
Rakano Cylix
Skycrag Cylix
Elysian Cylix
Xenan Cylix
Argenport Cylix

Since their introduction in [i]Argent Depths[/i], the Cylixes have collectively been some of the most well, powerful, power cards in Eternal, and we’ve seen access to them heavily dictate how popular certain faction combinations are in both Throne and Expedition. We’re pulling back a bit on their power level in 3-faction decks in particular by making them require a larger investment in their faction pairs to get the full value. 

[i]As always, cards you crafted that are nerfed will have the option of being destroyed for a full shiftstone refund.[/i]

[url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2-1-live-balance-update/]Buffs:[/url]
We’re also going to take this opportunity to buff some of the cards from Empire of Glass that haven’t seen as much play and give players some new avenues to explore some of the Bastion tribes.

[b]Matriarch Zende [/b]– Now 2/3 (was 2/2)

[b]Skimmer Wrangler[/b] – Now stuns two enemy units with flying (was 1).

[b]Opum's Technique [/b]– Now “Deal 5 damage to a factionless or multifaction enemy” (was “Deal 5 damage to a multifaction enemy”)

[url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2-1-live-balance-update/]Additional Fixes:[/url]
– Call on Allies, Align the Tesseract, and Clear the Way should now interact as expected with cards that count amplifications.

– The Speaking Circle should now play Display of Creation and Display of Destruction properly.


It’s been fantastic to see the community exploring the tower city of the Bastion, and we hope that these [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/2-1-live-balance-update/]changes[/url] will open up even more of the tower city to explore when [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/buried-memories/][i]Buried Memories[/i][/url] releases next week!

notes.title: 11/3 Balance Changes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/cc940894a9a95148dbd58be329e05508e1be36a3.jpg[/img]

With the conclusion of Eternal® Celebration came the Last Chance Qualifier for the 2020 Eternal World Championship, and while we saw a very diverse Throne field (congrats again to Doc28 for taking it down!), we feel it’s a great time for the next chapter of the format.

To open up space for the Throne format to continue to evolve, we’re making four straight-forward cost changes to the following cards:

[h2]Nerfs[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Severin of the Dark[/b] – Now 7SS (was 6SS)[/list]

An unchecked Severin can lead to some wild games, with huge lifesteal attacks and then a deck teeming with Destiny units. It’s sweet seeing Severin light up the board with these epic turns, but it can get old when the experience is too frequent. By upping its cost, we’re pulling back on just how often players will get griefed.

[list]
[*] [b]Blightmoth[/b] – Now 3SS (was 2SS)[/list]

When decks focus hard on playing lots of cheap units and exploiting fast tribal synergies, it’s important for other decks to have a satisfying variety of tools to select from to catch up. But when a card like Blightmoth proves so strong and ubiquitous it threatens not just to oppress x/1s from being viable but also the diversity of removal that appears. To that end, we’re bringing it more in line with other potential options by increasing its cost to three.

[i]Note: As with previous campaign changes, we are giving a one-time grant of 1,250 gold to users who purchased the Whispers of the Throne campaign. Users who upgraded the card will receive an additional 1,250 gold. As always, players will keep all their copies of Blightmoth.
[/i]
[list]
[*] [b]Turn to Seed[/b] – Now 4PP (was 3PP)[/list] 

Turn to Seed has been one of the most-played Primal cards since its printing, and we’d like to pull back on that ubiquity a little bit. Turn to Seed is a valuable tool against certain “all-in” strategies; however, when it’s the most common form of removal instead of a tactical weapon, it can start to threaten the place these exotic strategies have in the game. We’re hopeful that this change will preserve its strong anti-combo abilities, while also substantially decreasing the speed, ease, and frequency it shows up in more typical games.

[i]Note: As with previous campaign changes, we are giving a one-time grant of 1,250 gold to users who purchased the Shadow of the Spire campaign. Users who upgraded the card will receive an additional 1,250 gold. As always, players will keep all their copies of Turn to Seed.[/i]

[h2]Buffs[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Battle at the Gates[/b] – Now 3SS (was 4SS)[/list] 

A potentially epic comeback spell and fairly different form of interaction, at four-cost Battle at the Gates has yet to really break into the competitive metagame. We’re redrawing the battle lines to give this one another shot at the big time.

We’ll continue to monitor both Throne and Expedition as they get a big shakeup with Bastion Rising, and we hope that you’re as excited as we are for the 2020 Eternal World Championship later this month!

notes.title: Eternal Celebration
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/edf95a66dde1590caa7f42503ff5477ee012a13b.jpg[/img]

[h2]During the [i]Eternal[/i] Celebration, every player will be fully stocked with 4 copies of every card ever released!
[/h2]

[i]Eternal[/i]®’s fourth birthday is right around the corner and we’re starting the parteee early with a weeklong celebration in the run up to the $50,000 [i]Eternal[/i] World Championship!

From October 23 to November 1, the [i]Eternal[/i] Celebration is blowing the saloon doors off with events, cards, and cosmetics! There will be more announcements coming throughout next week, including new events (and new cards!), but at its core the [i]Eternal[/i] Celebration is about experiencing everything that [i]Eternal[/i] has to offer – both competitive and casual play, constructed and draft – and showing off the creativity and spirit of the community.

And everything is better with cards, so, first up:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/cccae9cc07d96a88604c3b207ddced8dcd162046.jpg[/img]
[h3]Limitless Possibilities![/h3]
[b]During the [i]Eternal[/i] Celebration, play for free with every card ever released![/b]

That’s right: Kick the tires on the deck of your dreams, or let the jank flow through you in the wildest piles imaginable in any constructed game mode…including the Last Chance Qualifier!

Crafting and destroying cards will be disabled during the Celebration, and when we all come to our senses at the end of the week, collections will return to their normal state. Any cards you acquire from packs or rewards, you’ll still keep. (You’ll still have your decklists, so you can craft any missing cards with the push of a button!)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/57f317c89e89024ef6b711b1b5737377bcbefd33.jpg[/img]
[h3][i]Eternal[/i] Celebration Queues & the Last Chance Qualifier![/h3]
A whopping FOUR seats for the 2020 Eternal World Championship will be up for grabs in a Last Chance Qualifier Event. Wanna play for your cut of $50,000? Brew up something new in the [i]Eternal[/i] Celebration and win your way to a seat at the top table!

Throughout the week, you can enter [i]Eternal[/i] Celebration Queues as often as you like. Each run costs 300 Gems or 4,000 Gold for 7 wins or 3 losses with your best Throne deck. (And, since you can play with every card in the game, this is a great chance to try something new!) Rack up a 7-win run, and you’ll be eligible to enter the weekend’s Last Chance Qualifier Event!

notes.title: 7/29 Balance Changes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/c64289d08b1d360938428e643acfc786375b3407.jpg[/img]

[h1]7/29 Balance Changes[/h1]

This live balance announcement is sooner than the originally planned middle of August patch; but when such a clear need for change arises as is the case with Rakano in Expedition (a strategy players have tuned to impressively high levels of performance, to the point of being extremely format-warping), our priority is to take action and address player concerns as quickly as we can. These changes will be going into effect tomorrow, July 29th. With the upcoming Expedition Challenge event this weekend, we carefully evaluated what select changes could best improve the format while not overly disrupting player’s preparations.

[h2]Nerfs[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Telut, The Iron Gate[/b] – Now “Surge: Your relic weapon gets +1/+1. Each enemy unit gets -1 strength this turn.” (was “Surge: Each enemy unit gets -1 strength and your relic weapon gets +1/+1.)[/list]

Telut’s ability permanently weakening enemy units was completely decimating entire strategies, frequently the turn he was played, having such a powerful impact, even removing him was too little too late. Now seeing widespread play beyond decks with relic weapons like Rakano Surge, Telut’s Surge ability has proven to be a major constraint on players looking to attack in the format. By adjusting Telut’s ability to work just for the turn, Telut should remain an enticing card to help your relic weapons or attackers, but open up more room for interaction making a bigger difference, as well as speeding up the pace of games.

[list]
[*][b]Ijin, Walking Armory[/b] –  Now “The first time you play another unit each turn, play a +4/+4 weapon on it.” (was “The first time you play a unit each turn, play a +4/+4 weapon on it.”)
[/list]

Ijin’s become more selfless and will now only play weapons on your other units. By playing a weapon immediately on herself when played if you had six Justice influence, she was asking too little of players for how much material she was bringing to the table. By needing to combine her with another unit, Ijin should less reliably be able to give immediate value without a lot of setup work, opening a larger window for possible counterplay before she’s able to.

We’ll be continuing to monitor the Expedition format as well as Throne and Draft following these changes to see if any further action is merited during our planned balance patch for the middle of August.

notes.title: June Balance Changes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/1a0f3fafd6837b5d5033e58ad1e96f732f2bc1b0.jpg[/img]

When we announced the mid-June balance patch last month, we weren’t sure if one would be needed or appropriate, with [url=https://www.direwolfdigital.com/news/new-set-argent-depths/][i]Argent Depths[/i] releasing next Tuesday[/url] and the Draft Preview beginning tomorrow. For starters, Throne is in a pretty good place (no strategy is overly dominant and no faction appears in more than half of the top ten archetypes); and we’re excited about what the upcoming set brings to the table. 

As for Expedition, the numbers point to the community having largely solved the most recent one; however, a brand new Expedition is coming with the release of Argent Depths, so we have decide to take this opportunity to primarily focus on a variety of buffs to interesting build around or niche cards that may not have gotten much of a chance in the spotlight. But first, the nerfs, all of which focus on aggressive Fire cards that have contributed to fire having a little too much resiliency stacked with charge:

[h2]Nerfs[/h2]
Tota Pioneer – Now 1/1 (was 1/2)
Thunder of Wings – Now creates a 4/1 Dragon. (Was a 4/2 Dragon)
Tota Pioneer is a powerful tool for Fire aggro decks looking to be better as games bog down. While not strictly charge, it can give virtual charge on account of playing it and using its ability in the same turn. While we’re big fans of the gameplay, we did want to restore some of the checks and balances around Fire decks that used to have more vulnerability in the form of 1-health units.

Thunder of Wings is likewise dropping a point of health to give it a little more vulnerability, given how hard and fast it hits.

[list]
[*] [b]Phoenix Stone[/b] – Now 1F and 3 to activate. (Was 2 cost and 2 to activate)
[*] [b]Pyre Elemental[/b] – Now cost is reduced by 3 if you’ve played a spell this turn. (Was cost reduced by 4)[/list]
Two major contributors to the powerful resiliency and charge damage of Fire aggro decks, both Phoenix Stone and Pyre Elemental were also contributing to Blazing Salvo’s overrepresentation (as well as leading to a lack of diversity among markets).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26908411/c144ce0f7c456c33a0fbd5886d1a0cf955ceeaef.jpg[/img]

Before getting into the buffs, we wanted to address a few recent cards that have been in a fair number of discussions, lately. First, Jekk, Mercenary Hunter has made major waves in both constructed formats, since his arrival last month. It is a strong card that can push a player further ahead or help them catch up against an early rush, and it’s definitely one we’ve been watching closely. The impact he’s had in Throne has been positive, and strategies appear to have been able to adapt quite effectively.

In Expedition, he’s had a much more pronounced defining impact, but with the Expedition changing shortly, we’re excited to see it in the context of the new format before making any decisions on it. We’ve definitely heard the feedback, and while we fully expect it to continue to be an excellent card, we’re hopeful that the new format might be better suited for him. That said, he’s very much a card we’ll be continuing to monitor closely in the days to come. 

Likewise, Turn to Seed, Silverblade Menace, and Auralian Supplier are also popular cards that we’re watching closely. With Turn to Seed, Primal got a great new tool for more counterplay against decks “all-in” on a specific unit. So far the numbers do not suggest it has proven imbalanced, and it has led to some innovative deckbuilding by players capitalizing on the “seeds” it provides, as well as contributing to a little bit more diversity among threats.

Silverblade Menace has been a great new option for players hoping for a big effect against those heavy-removal decks. While some feared it would kill control decks, instead we’ve seen a ton of adaptation and counterplay making for much more dramatic and exciting games, with more comebacks, as well as more incentive for the control decks to actually go for a win, instead of sitting around turn after turn. We’ll continue to watch for the risk of it being too decisive in games, but so far, it appears to have had a healthy impact on both formats.

Auralian Supplier’s power level has never been the real critique, but rather how much stronger it is on the play versus the draw. While it can be fun to set the card up, and it can help punish unitless strategies, if too much of the card’s power comes from the games you go first, that’s not great. So far, the numbers in throne do not suggest it imbalancing play vs draw in any meaningful way; however, in Expedition, it has been a little more swingy in this regard than we’d like. Again, we’d like to give the card a chance in the new format, but it’s definitely one we acknowledge could prove problematic, if things break in an unfortunate way.

[h2]Sidebuffs[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Rolant's Honor Guard[/b] – Now 6JJJ 5/5 (Was 7JJ 6/6)[/list]
As we prepare for some updates to the on-boarding campaign with Argent Depths, Rolant’s Honor Guard fits better in this new form. As always with any changes to cards that are not a strict buff, we will be offering refunds to any players who crafted copies.

[h2]Buffs[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Shield of the Line[/b] – Now pay 3 (was pay 4)
[*] [b]Ixtol’s Pendant[/b] – Now 1T (was 2T)
[*] [b]Panoptic Guardian[/b] – Now 4T (was 6T)
[*] [b]Ixtol, Champion of Grodov[/b] – Now 5T (was 6TTT)
[*] [b]Fencing Master[/b] – Now 2/3 (was 2/2)
[*] [b]Minsod, the Peerless[/b] – Now 7J (was 8JJ)
[*] [b]Snowdrift Delver[/b] – Now 2/3 (was 2/2)
[*] [b]South-Wind Herald[/b] – Now 3/3 makes a 10/10 (was 3/2 Makes a 9/9)
[*] [b]Skyward Seer[/b] – Now 3PP (was 4PP)
[*] [b]North-Wind Herald[/b] – Now 4/2 (was 3/2)
[*] [b]Lunging Wisp[/b] – Now 1S (was 2S)
[*] [b]Noxious Wvyrach[/b] – Now 6SS (was 7SS)
[*] [b]Harga, Armory Warden[/b] – Now 2TJ (was 3TJ)
[*] [b]Aamri, Dragonbane[/b] – Now 5JJJTTT (was 6JJJTTT)
[/list]
This list contains quite a few oddballs, but we’re hopeful that every card on this list has some purpose for some players and we’re excited to experiment with this wide mix of buffs to underplayed cards.

We’re looking forward to Argent Depths coming soon and will check in again on any potential balance changes mid-July.
